statement: Let V be the set of all values occurring in pairs, and let P = {{x_i,y_i} : 0 <= i < len(pairs)}. Let N be the number of rooted trees T on the vertex set V such that for every two distinct x,y in V, the unordered pair {x,y} belongs to P if and only if x is an ancestor of y or y is an ancestor of x in T. (Here an ancestor of a node is a node on the root-to-node path excluding the node itself; equivalently N is the number of parent maps on V forming a rooted tree with this ancestor-comparability relation.) The function returns a result r and r = 0 if N = 0, r = 1 if N = 1, and r = 2 if N >= 2.
preconditions: pairs is nonempty; for every i with 0 <= i < len(pairs), pairs[i] has length 2; writing pairs[i] = [x_i,y_i], 1 <= x_i < y_i <= 500; and the unordered pairs {x_i,y_i} are pairwise distinct.

statement: The function returns a result r, i.e. it does not fail with arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds access, or a panic.
preconditions: pairs is nonempty; for every i with 0 <= i < len(pairs), pairs[i] has length 2; writing pairs[i] = [x_i,y_i], 1 <= x_i < y_i <= 500; and the unordered pairs {x_i,y_i} are pairwise distinct.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is one of 0, 1, or 2.
preconditions: pairs is nonempty; for every i with 0 <= i < len(pairs), pairs[i] has length 2; writing pairs[i] = [x_i,y_i], 1 <= x_i < y_i <= 500; and the unordered pairs {x_i,y_i} are pairwise distinct.

pairs is nonempty; for every i with 0 <= i < len(pairs), pairs[i] has length 2; writing pairs[i] = [x_i,y_i], 1 <= x_i < y_i <= 500; and the unordered pairs {x_i,y_i} are pairwise distinct. Let V be the set of all values occurring in pairs, and let P be the set of unordered pairs {x_i,y_i}. The graph G=(V,P) has no universal vertex: for every v in V there exists u in V with u != v and {u,v} not in P.

pairs is nonempty; for every i with 0 <= i < len(pairs), pairs[i] has length 2; writing pairs[i] = [x_i,y_i], 1 <= x_i < y_i <= 500; and the unordered pairs {x_i,y_i} are pairwise distinct. Let V be the set of all values occurring in pairs, and let P be the set of unordered pairs {x_i,y_i}. The graph G=(V,P) is complete: |V| >= 2 and P is the set of all unordered pairs of distinct elements of V.

pairs is nonempty; for every i with 0 <= i < len(pairs), pairs[i] has length 2; writing pairs[i] = [x_i,y_i], 1 <= x_i < y_i <= 500; and the unordered pairs {x_i,y_i} are pairwise distinct. Let V be the set of all values occurring in pairs, and let P be the set of unordered pairs {x_i,y_i}. There is a vertex c and a set L such that V = {c} union L, c is not in L, |L| >= 2, and P = {{c,l} : l in L} with no other pairs.

statement: Let r be the result of check_ways(pairs) and r' be the result of check_ways(pairs'). Both calls return and r = r'.
preconditions: Both pairs and pairs' satisfy the problem constraints: each is nonempty, every element is a two-element vector [x,y] with 1 <= x < y <= 500, and all unordered pairs in each slice are pairwise distinct. Moreover, pairs and pairs' contain exactly the same set of unordered pairs, possibly in different orders.

statement: Whenever the function returns r = 1, the graph G=(V,P) has exactly one universal vertex: there is a unique v in V such that {v,u} is in P for every u in V with u != v.
preconditions: pairs is nonempty; for every i with 0 <= i < len(pairs), pairs[i] has length 2; writing pairs[i] = [x_i,y_i], 1 <= x_i < y_i <= 500; and the unordered pairs {x_i,y_i} are pairwise distinct. Let V be the set of all values occurring in pairs, and let P be the set of unordered pairs {x_i,y_i}.

statement: There exist two distinct parent maps on V, both having root u, such that in each resulting rooted tree, for every two distinct x,y in V, the pair {x,y} is in P if and only if x is an ancestor of y or y is an ancestor of x.
preconditions: pairs satisfies the problem constraints: it is nonempty, every element is a two-element vector [x,y] with 1 <= x < y <= 500, and all unordered pairs are distinct. Let V be the set of all values occurring in pairs and P the set of unordered pairs from pairs. Suppose the function returns r = 2 and the graph G=(V,P) has exactly one universal vertex u, meaning u is the unique element of V with {u,v} in P for every v in V with v != u.

pairs is nonempty; every pairs[i] has length 2; writing pairs[i]=[x_i,y_i], 1 <= x_i < y_i <= 500; all unordered pairs {x_i,y_i} are distinct. Let V be the occurring values, P the unordered pairs, and suppose G=(V,P) has at least two universal vertices. Suppose check_ways(pairs) returns r with r != 0.

statement: Every rooted tree on V satisfying the ancestor-comparability condition for P has root u; equivalently, all valid trees are rooted at the unique universal vertex u.
preconditions: pairs is nonempty; every pairs[i] has length 2; writing pairs[i]=[x_i,y_i], 1 <= x_i < y_i <= 500; all unordered pairs {x_i,y_i} are distinct. Let V be the occurring values and P the unordered pairs. Suppose G=(V,P) has a unique universal vertex u, and suppose check_ways(pairs) returns a nonzero result r.
